purpose: Rehearse typed command mirroring from one Quest Termux agent to another through the fleet controller.
authority_boundary: Quest A submits typed mirror intents only.
Quest B remains the final execution authority through its local mirror binding policy.
The controller owns mirror leases, intent state, idempotency mapping, and result correlation.
Peer gossip remains status-only and does not carry commands, shell text, ADB targets, pairing data, install requests, or launch requests.
Both headsets initiate outbound controller traffic; no headset listener is exposed to the internet.
ADB-backed commands still require the target-side loopback ADB shell gate.

preflight.label: boundary
preflight.command: Review docs/mirror-protocol-boundary.md and confirm the run is typed-command mirroring, not raw control.

preflight.label: controller
preflight.command: Start the fleet controller with mirror routes enabled.

preflight.label: target-policy
preflight.command: Review the target agent mirror_bindings config for source, lease, command kind, component, scenario, TTL, and visible-session settings.

start.label: start-agents
start.command: Run source and target Termux fleet agents against the controller.

start.label: submit-intent
start.command: Submit a mirror-command-intent for agent.status before any ADB-backed action.

status.label: target-result
status.command: Confirm the target posts a fleet-command-result and the controller maps it back to the mirror intent.

status.label: mirror-events
status.command: Read /api/mirror/v1/sessions/{lease_id}/events and confirm queued and terminal states are present.

stop.label: revoke-lease
stop.command: POST to /api/mirror/v1/leases/{lease_id}/revoke and confirm later intents are rejected.

cleanup.label: no-listeners
cleanup.command: Confirm no headset-side ADB, VNC, HTTP, or Termux listener was exposed.

cleanup.label: public-boundary
cleanup.command: Keep real headset names, serials, logs, screenshots, pairing data, package IDs, and network addresses out of public artifacts.

risks.risk: Mirroring can drift into unrestricted remote control.
risks.recovery: Keep Quest A as an intent source, enforce Quest B local policy, and reject raw shell, raw ADB, and coordinate mirroring.

risks.risk: Peer gossip could accidentally become a command transport.
risks.recovery: Keep gossip validators rejecting command-like fields and route mirror commands through the controller.

risks.risk: ADB-backed mirror commands can execute without a current target shell lease.
risks.recovery: Require the target agent to verify uid=2000(shell) before bounded ADB-backed executors run.

notes: The synthetic examples intentionally avoid real headset IDs, serials, LAN IPs, pairing material, logs, and screenshots.
